data.narrative:
MacroFab is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $141M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public and eight private—spanning the same sector and overlapping funding stages, including late-stage peers such as Exotec (Series D, $2.0B) and stage-matched comparables like Hadrian and Nimble Robotics (both Series C, $1.6B and $1.0B respectively).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses the $141M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implying a valuation of $240M. The peer-median method anchors to five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B, range $1.0B–$2.0B. This reflects valuations from Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), and Exotec ($2.0B, Series D).

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $204M to $1.9B, with a median of $945M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around MacroFab's growth trajectory relative to peers. Key sensitivities include revenue scale and unit economics relative to the Hadrian and Nimble Robotics cohort, as well as timing assumptions embedded in the stage-progression method.
